title: Latency-budget-aware queue pruner and weighted admission
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce a latency-budget-aware queue pruning mechanism plus a weighted admission controller that enforces regional quotas and supports graceful trimming of responses. The feature aims to protect P99 SLOs during cross-region load spikes by prioritizing requests, pruning queued work proactively, and offering progressive degradation modes (token trimming, model fallback, early partial responses).
background: We currently rely on token-bucket and simple priority lanes for tenant-level protection, but during multi-region storms we see queue growth that violates P99 latency SLOs and causes broad customer impact. Existing shedding approaches are coarse-grained and cause either excessive rejections or over-eager fallbacks. Operators need a predictable, observable strategy that ties admission decisions to remaining latency budget and region-level capacity budgets.
goals: 1) Keep end-to-end P99 latency within configured SLOs for high-priority tenants during region-level overloads. 2) Provide smooth degradation modes that minimize catastrophic failures (500s) and maximize delivered utility (partial responses). 3) Allow regional quota decay and burst reconstitution to support short spikes without long tail throttling. 4) Expose clear metrics and traces for post-incident analysis.
non_goals: 1) This work does not replace global capacity planning. 2) It does not implement full cross-region live migration of warm KV cache. 3) It is not a billing change — cost accounting is out of scope.
design_overview: Two coordinated components: (A) Queue Pruner: continuously evaluates pending requests in per-shard priority queues and evicts or trims requests based on a computed remaining latency budget and per-tenant region quota. (B) Weighted Admitter: an admission controller that calculates per-request admission probability using tenant weight, SLA class, and recent success credits. Admission decisions support deterministic graceful degradation modes: token_trim, model_fallback, and early_partial_response.
admission_algorithm: 1) Compute remaining latency budget: SLO_ms - elapsed_ms - safety_buffer_ms. 2) Estimate queueing and service time for candidate request using recent histogram for route/model/seq_len. 3) If estimated_completion > remaining_budget: consult degradation policy ordered by least-impactful to application (token_trim -> model_fallback -> partial_response). 4) If no degradation acceptable, apply probabilistic rejection based on tenant weight and region_available_credits. 5) Admission probabilities decay linearly as credits approach zero and recover with configured half-life. All decisions are annotated with trace tags for downstream debugging.
degradation_modes: token_trim: truncate generation to N tokens or to a token-budget percentage
model_fallback: route to a cheaper compatible model variant (quantized or smaller) with adjusted prompt
early_partial_response: return partial content with metadata indicating truncation and suggested retry/handoff
noop_reject: deterministic hard reject when tenant is over explicit quota and no graceful mode is allowed
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated per-region and per-cluster. 2) Start in dry-run mode for a single non-critical region for 48h (observe metrics, traces, and false-positive degradation). 3) Enable probabilistic admission (1%) in production region for 24h. 4) If metrics stable, ramp to 10% then 50% then 100% over 2 weeks. 5) For tenants with high SLA, enable 'conservative mode' (higher safety buffer) by default unless tenant opts in. 6) Post-rollout: monitor and run canary failure injection tests.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission logic, mocked latency budgets, and degradation selection. Integration tests simulating queue growth with synthetic load harness across multi-region testbed. Chaos tests: region isolation, KV cache cold-start, CPU/GPU slower degradation. Load tests to verify P99 improvements compared to baseline. E2E tests verifying trace annotations and correct fallback headers returned to clients.
acceptance_criteria: Enables feature flag and run in dry-run without causing rejects
In controlled overload tests, P99 improves by >= 20% relative to baseline for prioritized tenants
Degradation decisions are present in traces and show expected mode ordering
No unhandled 5xx surge after enabling at 10% traffic in production region
Dashboards and alerts built for new metrics and reviewed by SRE
risks: Over-aggressive pruning may lead to user-facing quality regressions; mitigate with conservative defaults and canary ramping.
Estimates for service time may be skewed for new model versions, causing under/over admission; include model-versioned histograms and fallback thresholds.
Cross-region credit coordination introduces complexity; ensure eventual consistency but accept temporary divergence during partitions.
Increased observability volume (traces/annotations) may raise costs; sample traces and limit high-cardinality tags to tenant IDs only when opted-in for debug.
notes: Prototype validated in staging with 10k rps synthetic spike. Observed 27% reduction in P99 for premium tenants when token_trim + model_fallback allowed. Next steps: finalize API for per-tenant degradation policy and surface a 'grace_score' to client SDKs so applications can choose to re-request fuller responses.
